title: Best of Italy
blurb: Rome, Florence, Venice, Assisi and Sorrento in ten nights, with Capri, Pompeii and a gondola ride along the way.
pace: Full days on the move, with free afternoons in Rome, Sorrento and Capri
inclusions:
Ten nights in hotels, three of them at Villa Pamphili in Rome
Ten breakfasts, one lunch and five dinners
Travel Director throughout
Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel and the Colosseum with a local guide
A choice in Florence: the Accademia to see Michelangelo’s David, or a walk and a café stop with your Travel Director
Leatherwork and goldsmithing demonstration in Florence
Private boat through Venice, a gondola ride and a glassblowing workshop
Basilica of St Francis in Assisi with a local guide
Boat to Capri and a walk through Capri town
Pompeii with a local guide
Farm lunch at Casa Barone on the slopes of Vesuvius
Farewell dinner in Rome with wine and a private opera performance
erics_note:
This is the Insight tour I suggest when someone wants Rome, Florence and Venice and the south as well. It adds Assisi, two nights in Sorrento with a day on Capri, and Pompeii on the way back to Rome, so you see most of the country in eleven days. Most stops are two nights, and the hotel in Venice is central, which means you can walk out after the day visitors have gone.

It is a full itinerary. There are long drives from Florence to Venice by way of Pisa, and from Assisi down to Sorrento. The Rome hotel, Villa Pamphili, sits beside a large park rather than in the centre. If you would rather slow down and spend longer in fewer places, ask me about a custom journey.

itinerary.title: Arrive in Rome
itinerary.text: Settle in, then meet your Travel Director and the group for dinner at a local restaurant.

itinerary.title: The Vatican and ancient Rome
itinerary.text: With a local guide, the Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel, then St Peter’s Basilica from outside. Across the Tiber, the Circus Maximus, the Arch of Constantine and a guided visit to the Colosseum. The rest of the day is free. If Vatican tickets are unavailable, the Capitoline Museums take their place.

itinerary.title: Through Chianti to Florence
itinerary.text: North from Rome through Lazio and the Chianti hills to Florence. Dinner at a local restaurant.

itinerary.title: Florence
itinerary.text: Your choice: the Accademia and Michelangelo’s David, or a walk with your Travel Director and a stop at a local café. Then the cathedral, the bell tower, the Baptistery and Piazza della Signoria on foot, and a demonstration of leatherwork and goldsmithing.

itinerary.title: Pisa, then Venice
itinerary.text: The Leaning Tower, the cathedral and the baptistery in the Square of Miracles, then across the Apennines and Emilia-Romagna to Venice. Dinner at a local restaurant.

itinerary.title: Venice
itinerary.text: A private boat past churches and palaces to St Mark’s Square, a walk past the Bridge of Sighs and the Doge’s Palace, a gondola ride, and a visit to a glassblowing workshop.

itinerary.title: Assisi
itinerary.text: The Church of St Mary of the Angels in the valley, then the upper town with a local guide and the Basilica of St Francis, with Giotto’s frescoes. Free time in town. Dinner is included.

itinerary.title: South to Sorrento
itinerary.text: South past Cassino, then along the coast road to Sorrento, above the Bay of Naples. The rest of the day is free.

itinerary.title: Capri
itinerary.text: A boat across the bay to Marina Grande, up to Capri town for a walk with a local guide, then the funicular down and back to Sorrento. The rest of the day is free.

itinerary.title: Pompeii, Vesuvius and Rome
itinerary.text: A guided walk through the excavations at Pompeii, then lunch at Casa Barone, a family farm on Vesuvius that grows Piennolo tomatoes. On to Rome for a farewell dinner with wine and a private opera performance.
